test_title: SSC CHSL Tier-1 2023: Official Paper (Held On: 03 Aug, 2023 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Which of these statements is INCORRECT about Human Development Index?

options.text: The level of education is represented in the HDI
It uses the per capita GDP of a country on purchasing power parity terms to represent the income component.
Birth rate and death rate important components of the HDI
Life expectancy at birth is one of the components of the HDI.

solution:
The correct answer is __**Birth rate and death rate important components of the HDI.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Human Development Index (HDI)** is a measure of **human development **that takes into account three dimensions: **health, education, and income.**
 
• The level of education is one of the components of the HDI, along with the **years of schooling **and the expected years of schooling.
 
• The income component of the HDI is represented by the **per capita GDP **of a country on **purchasing power parity terms**, which takes into account the differences in the cost of living between countries.
 
• **Life expectancy **at birth is another component of the HDI, as it reflects the** overall health **and well-being of a population.
 
• Birth rate and death rate are **not components** of the HDI, as they are considered to be** demographic indicators** rather than measures of human development.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The HDI was developed by the** United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) **in **1990** as a way to measure progress in human development across countries.
 
• The HDI ranges from **0 to 1**, with higher values indicating **higher levels of human development.**
 
• The HDI is updated annually and is widely used by **policymakers, researchers, and advocates** to track progress in human development and identify areas for improvement.
 
• Other measures of human development include the** Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI),** which takes into account a broader range of dimensions of poverty beyond income, and the **Gender Development Index (GDI)**, which measures gender gaps in education, health, and income.
